transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

What brings me in is that I keep getting hit out of nowhere with the scene of my cousin on that pavement. It's like... I can hear the shouting and see the lights all over again, even when I'm just standing in the church office trying to act normal. It just comes back to me, clear as day.
What happened to your cousin on the pavement?

I... I don't really want to go into the exact details of it today. It was just a really bad situation. I just remember the aftermath, you know, the shouting and the flashing lights, and... he was just lying there. I'd rather not talk about the specifics of what actually happened to him, if that's alright. It's just too hard.
How long have you been experiencing these memories of your cousin on the pavement?
It's... well, this has been going on since he was killed. That was two years and three months ago.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of your cousin?

Yeah, I do. I actually take the long way around town now, just so I don't have to pass the community center or that court. And if people... if somebody starts talking about that night, I just shut it down, or I find a reason to leave the room. I just can't be around it.
Do you have trouble sleeping or find yourself easily startled?
No, not really. I mean... my sleep is mostly fine, I think. And I wouldn't say I get startled easily, either. I just haven't really noticed either of those things being an issue for me.
Do you often feel guilty, ashamed, or angry about what happened to your cousin?

Yeah, I do. Honestly, most days I just feel this... this heavy mix of fear, anger, and guilt sitting right in my chest from the minute I wake up. I just feel like I failed God, my family, and the kids who trusted me. It's just a constant feeling.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I really have. I used to love preaching, playing the keys... taking pictures, and just running with the guys on the court. But now, I mostly just go through the motions. Or I avoid it altogether. It just... none of it feels alive in me anymore.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when these memories come back?
No, I don't think so. When the memories hit, I'm... I'm definitely still in my own body. If anything, I just feel stuck in it. But no, I haven't ever felt like I was watching myself from the outside.
Do you ever feel numb or detached from the world around you when you're not having those memories of your cousin?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed feeling numb or... disconnected from things. Like I said, I feel a lot of heavy stuff all day, but I'm definitely still feeling it. I wouldn't say I feel detached from the world around me.
Do you try to push away or avoid thinking about your cousin when the memories aren't happening on their own?

Yeah, I do. I actually... I take the long way around town now, just so I don't have to pass the community center or that court. And if someone brings it up—like if somebody starts talking about that night—I just shut it down. Or I'll find a reason to leave. I just try to avoid it as much as I can.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now find that you have lost interest in them most of the time?

Yeah, a lot of things, actually. I used to really love preaching, playing the keys... taking pictures. I used to love running with the guys on the court, too. But now, I mostly just go through the motions if I have to do them, or... or I just avoid it altogether. None of it really feels alive in me anymore. I just don't have the interest.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?
No, not really. I can't think of anything I look forward to anymore. It's just... everything feels pretty flat right now. I just don't get any enjoyment out of things like I used to.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to, even if it's just a little?
No, like I said, there's really nothing. I just... I don't get any joy out of anything right now. It's all just empty.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find some pleasure in, even if it's not as much as before?

I... I really don't know how else to say it, but no. There isn't anything. Like I mentioned a minute ago, the things I actually used to love doing—preaching, playing the keys, taking pictures, running the court with the guys—I just avoid them now, or I just go through the motions if I absolutely have to. None of it feels alive in me anymore. I really don't find pleasure in any of it.
Have you ever thought about harming yourself since your cousin's death?
No. No, I haven't. I mean, things are hard, and I feel empty a lot of the time, but I haven't ever thought about hurting myself. That's not something that's crossed my mind.
Are there any days when you feel like doing the things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. Like I was just saying... there aren't any days where I wake up and actually want to do those things. Every day is pretty much the same. I just don't have the desire to do any of it anymore.
Are there any days when you feel like doing the things you used to enjoy, even if it's just for a short time?
No, not even for a short time. Like I said, it's just... it's gone. I don't have those moments where the spark comes back, even for a minute. It's just a flat feeling all the time.
Have your symptoms lasted for more than two years since your cousin's death?
Yeah, it has. This has been going on since my cousin was killed... that was two years and three months ago. So, yes, it's been a bit over two years now.
